newsitem.title: USA: Prudential settlement decision seen after March 3.
newsitem.headline: Prudential settlement decision seen after March 3.

text.p: A U.S. federal judge is expected to issue a decision on the fairness of a proposed Prudential Insurance Co of America class-action settlement sometime after March 3.
At a hearing in Newark, U.S. District Judge Alfred Wolin said he would accept additional filings on the Prudential case no later than 1600 EST (2100 GMT) on March 3.
"We really want to decide this issue," he said, saying he would issue a decision promptly. The proposed settlement must win the judge's approval before it can go into effect.

Under the proposed settlement, Prudential will pay at least $410 million to holders of as many 10.7 million policies purchased between 1982 and 1995 to settle claims that it used deceptive practices to sell life insurance.
At the daylong hearing, Prudential and an attorney representing the members of the class action defended the settlement as fair.
Several people objected to the settlement, expressing concern that the process allowing eligible policyholders to participate in the program might be too complicated for some of them.
Susan Chin, the daughter of one policyholder, said her elderly father did not understand English and had difficulty understanding what to do.
In addition, she said a toll-free number established to provide policyholders with assistance gave misinformation.

Prudential and the attorney representing the class-action members said additional information will be published in a number of foreign language newspapers and apologized for the trouble with the toll-free number.
Prudential also said it would establish a separate toll-free number to provide people with necessary information about their policies.
